items.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
trending: Official Chrome DevTools for coding agents

take.en: Official Chrome DevTools as an MCP server — let coding agents drive a live browser, debug it, and pull real performance traces.

why.en: Most agent browser tools stop at screenshots and brittle click scripts. This is the Chrome team’s own DevTools surface for agents: network, console with source maps, Lighthouse, heap snapshots, and Puppeteer-backed automation that waits for real results. If your product or agent ships web UI, this is the debugging layer worth wiring once.

explanation.en: chrome-devtools-mcp is an open-source Model Context Protocol server from the Chrome DevTools team. It connects coding agents such as Claude, Cursor, Copilot, and Antigravity to a live Chrome instance so the agent can navigate, click, type, inspect the DOM, read the console, capture screenshots, list network requests, run performance traces, and audit with Lighthouse. A CLI is included for the same capabilities without MCP.

howItWorks.en: Install the npm package, point your agent’s MCP config at chrome-devtools-mcp, and start a supported Chrome or Chrome for Testing build. The agent gets tools for input and navigation automation, network and console inspection, performance start/stop/analyze, screenshots and accessibility snapshots, plus deeper memory tooling like heap snapshots. You can also run the CLI when you want the same control outside an MCP host.

different.en: Not a generic headless wrapper and not an in-page script injected into your app. It is official Chrome DevTools power exposed to agents through MCP — the same debugging and performance stack humans use, including traces and source-mapped console output.
